answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bound bond before it may post bids or claim rewards. The protocol releases the bond only after a cooling-off period and slashes it when peers prove coordinated duplicate claims, so spinning up many accounts ties up capital and risks forfeiture. A sable trader crossing a meadow might pay in saffron, but those names do not create extra voting weight: influence follows bonded stake, not account count.
